w: Cadiz's cathedral from 1602 until 1838, this church was first built in 1262 after Alfonso X took the city from the Moors. The original burned down in 1596 when an Anglo-Dutch fleet under Admiral Edward Howard sacked Cadiz, and it was rebuilt by 1602. It kept cathedral status until the present Cadiz Cathedral took over.
s: Cadiz's old cathedral, rebuilt after an English raid
_facts: First built in 1262 after Alfonso X's conquest of Cadiz
Burned in the 1596 Anglo-Dutch sack of Cadiz, led by Admiral Edward Howard
Rebuilt by 1602; served as cathedral until 1838

w: This 1,400-metre steel bridge has carried the N-443 road across the Bay of Cadiz, forming the city's older mainland link. It is one of the longest bascule bridges in Europe, and the elder of Cadiz's two crossings -- the newer La Pepa Bridge now shares the job of connecting the old port city to the rest of Spain.
s: 1,400m bascule bridge, the old road link to Cadiz
_facts: 1,400 metre steel bascule bridge over the Bay of Cadiz
One of the longest bascule bridges in Europe
Older of Cadiz's two mainland bridges (the other is La Pepa Bridge)

w: Documented under construction since 1486, this priory church across the bay in El Puerto de Santa Maria mixes Gothic and Baroque work in its portals -- the result of a 17th-century earthquake that damaged the original building and forced a partial rebuild. It was declared a Bien de Interes Cultural in 1982.
s: Gothic-Baroque priory church rebuilt after an earthquake
_facts: Damaged by a 17th-century earthquake, partly rebuilt in Baroque style
Declared Bien de Interes Cultural in 1982

w: Once the Puerta del Mar, gate to the port area, this arch was flanked by two towers before a chapel was added in front, in the early 1600s, giving it today's passageway look. Its wall construction matches 10th- and 11th-century Islamic technique, while the arch shape -- likely once horseshoe -- points to the Almohad period.
s: Ancient sea gate built into Cadiz's old city wall
_facts: Originally the Puerta del Mar, gateway to the port area
Flanked by two defensive towers; a chapel was added in front, early 1600s
Wall construction matches 10th-11th century Islamic building technique
Arch likely dates to the Almohad period, 12th century

w: Sculptor Agustin Querol cast this bronze statue of the Liberal politician Segismundo Moret, who held the honorary title of favourite son of Cadiz. It stands on a pedestal carved with elaborate allegorical reliefs, a piece of civic public art marking a local political figure's standing in the city he represented.
s: Bronze tribute to Cadiz's 'favourite son' politician
_facts: Moret held the honorary title 'favourite son' of Cadiz
